title: Cold showers benefits
summary: NH shares five years of daily cold showers: he separates cold showers from ice baths, argues showers don't hurt protein synthesis (he gained ~40 lb while taking them), and recommends them for tendon recovery, sleep, possibly fat distribution, and above all mental fortitude. He covers how to start, timing after training vs before bed, and contrast showers.

claims.claim: Cold showers are a fitness urban legend with little real science; claims range from miracle cure to harmful, giving them a mystical aura.
He distinguishes cold showers from cold baths and ice baths, which he has never done and doesn't speak about.
Critics say cold exposure blunts protein synthesis, promotes inflammation and may stress the cardiovascular system.
His football coach taught him to rinse sore, heavy legs with very cold water after training, which made them feel better.
After moving to a much colder country, he started cold showers before bed to prepare his body for the harsh winters.
Starting lifting around age 20, he rinsed with the coldest water available after training because hot water felt terrible when already warm.
Be careful researching on 4chan: much of what's posted is false or deliberate trolling, and many YouTube fitness practices originated there as jokes.
In his experience cold showers help recovery, especially sore tendons, which feel much better as blood rushes back in.
The argument that post-training cold disrupts the beneficial inflammation process mostly comes from studies on long cold or ice-bath immersion that really drop body temperature.
Cold showers only chill the surface briefly; the body rushes blood back and you rewarm quickly, so he doesn't believe they impair protein synthesis.
He gained about 40 lb from age 20 to 25 while taking cold showers daily, so they likely don't damage muscle growth.
He has taken a cold shower every single day for five years without interruption and can't go without them now.
A cold shower before bed improves sleep quality by lowering body temperature, especially useful on hot summer nights.
Before bed, let cold water hit the legs, upper chest and upper back, then wipe off without fully drying and go to bed; you sleep better and don't sweat.
He kept taking cold showers even in winters below -20 degrees, which is much harder on the psyche.
Living in a cold environment burns more calories and influences how the body stores fat.
Reportedly (no science cited) cold exposure promotes brown fat, stored on the male chest and upper back, possibly reducing waist fat storage.
The body would prefer fat over the chest and upper back to protect the lungs and heart from cold; for a bodybuilder that beats fat on the waist.
He naturally stores lots of fat on his chest and upper back, possibly linked to starting cold showers at 20, but can't confirm a difference.
You can't spot-reduce fat, but cold showers might nudge fat distribution toward muscles rather than organs or waist; worth trying for stubborn fat.
The most underrated benefit of cold showers is mental fortitude: they trigger fight-or-flight and anxious anticipation you learn to overcome.
Start gradually; tap water at home isn't that cold, but stream water is much colder and gives less time to adapt.
Start with the body, then the head; cold water on the face triggers a much stronger, exhilarating fight-or-flight reaction.
After training, keep it short: a contrast-style blast of cold for about a minute while warm, not long enough to chill to the bone.
Before bed, stay in the cold shower until you start shivering a little so the body is properly cooled down.
Contrast showers alternate very hot and very cold; cold pulls blood to the organs, heat sends it to the skin, which is good for circulation.
Contrast showers are reportedly risky for people with weak hearts, but Scandinavian and Japanese hot-to-cold bathing habits don't show many heart attacks, so be cautious but you should be fine.
Only do contrast showers once you are used to very cold showers.
He suspects cold showers affect hormonal profile and wouldn't be surprised if they boost testosterone.
Cold showers are a free habit that builds mental strength and aids recovery; once established you don't think twice about it.
